issue: After Kisor v. Wilkie, must courts defer to Sentencing Guidelines commentary that directs use of the greater of actual or intended loss under USSG § 2B1.1, or may they reject that commentary-based rule?

sides.position: Courts still defer to § 2B1.1 commentary directing use of intended loss (greater of actual or intended loss) even after Kisor, so the commentary controls unless plainly erroneous.
cases: United States v. Nock, 148 F.4th 607 (8th Cir. 2025)
United States v. Holthaus, 486 F.3d 451 (8th Cir. 2007)
United States v. Currie, No. 25-2666, 25-3141 (8th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: After Kisor, courts should not defer to the § 2B1.1 commentary on intended loss, so the Guideline's text alone governs loss calculation (the position the defendants urged).

this_court: defers to the commentary and follows Nock; the court holds that intended loss may be considered and does not resolve the split, noting the Supreme Court has granted certiorari in Beaird v. United States
quote: Supreme Court has granted certiorari to consider a circuit split on this issue.
cite: United States v. Latroy Currie, No. 25-2666, 25-3141 (8th Cir. 2026)
